title: The Byrock Story
description: A curated, investigational account of Byrock Technologies, its equine laminitis program, and the path from scientific insight to further development.

nodes.title: Byrock Technologies
nodes.summary: Byrock Technologies is a biotechnology company focused on translating scientific insight into practical veterinary innovation. Its current public story centers on equine laminitis and PTP-102, an investigational therapy being developed for continued study.

media.alt: Dark premium biotech cover visual with the Byrock Technologies identity, subtle cyan linework, and a connection between equine health and therapeutic science.

nodes.title: The Unmet Need in Laminitis
nodes.summary: Laminitis is a serious inflammatory condition affecting the tissues that support the hoof. It can cause severe pain, lameness, structural damage, loss of function, and in severe cases euthanasia, leaving owners, veterinarians, and equine professionals in need of better options while the condition’s complexity remains clear.

media.alt: Illustrated horse profile with the hoof region highlighted in a restrained clinical infographic style.

nodes.title: The Scientific Rationale
nodes.summary: Byrock’s approach is based on the hypothesis that modulating inflammatory mediators, metalloprotease activity, oxidative stress, and related tissue injury may help reduce lamellar damage in laminitis. PTP-102 is an investigational candidate designed to intervene in those processes; this is a scientific rationale under active study, not a final clinical conclusion.

media.alt: Simplified mechanism diagram showing inflammatory and tissue-damaging pathways involved in laminitis with an investigational intervention point.

nodes.title: From PTP-100 to PTP-102
nodes.summary: The laminitis program evolved through three scientific generations: PTP-100, an early antibody-based concept rooted in camel heavy-chain antibody technology; PTP-101, a synthetic peptide approach aimed at metalloprotease inhibition; and PTP-102, described in company materials as a synthetic nonglucocorticoid 21-aminosteroid and methylated tirilazad. The sequence represents scientific refinement, not commercial progression or approval.

media.alt: Three-step timeline showing the evolution of the Byrock laminitis platform from PTP-100 through PTP-101 to PTP-102.

nodes.title: Research Evidence to Date
nodes.summary: Company materials describe in-vitro work, in-vivo pilot work, and supporting internal reports related to induced acute laminitis models. The public evidence narrative should describe the direction of early findings carefully, acknowledge study design and sample-size limitations, and avoid presenting developmental research as conclusive clinical proof.

media.alt: Three-panel research overview summarizing in-vitro work, pilot in-vivo work, and study reports supporting ongoing PTP-102 development.

nodes.title: Regulatory Pathway
nodes.summary: PTP-102 is investigational and is being advanced through a staged veterinary development and regulatory pathway. Byrock’s work includes refining the evidence package, study strategy, manufacturing considerations, and product development plan; further evidence and documentation remain important before any approval or market availability could be discussed.

media.alt: Development milestone ladder showing research, study planning, regulatory engagement, further evidence generation, and a future commercialization pathway.

nodes.title: How the Program Is Being Studied
nodes.summary: The program is being developed through staged studies that consider relevant horse populations, treatment timing, clinical observations, time-based follow-up, and outcome measures such as lameness assessment, hoof-related findings, and tissue or biomarker analyses where appropriate. Broader validation, larger-scale evidence, and continued development work are still required before definitive claims can be made.

media.alt: Clinical study flow diagram showing horse selection, treatment timing, observation windows, outcome assessment, and follow-up.

nodes.title: The Team Behind Byrock
nodes.summary: Byrock brings together founder-led scientific vision, medical and development leadership, and commercial, strategic, project, and corporate support. The public team story should use approved job titles and concise biographies, with Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, presented as Founder and Inventor.

nodes.title: Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD
nodes.summary: Founder and inventor Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, has a longstanding background in microbiology, genetics, virology, antiviral development, antibody science, and biotechnology venture creation. His earlier work, as documented in the dated CV source, provides foundational biography for the Byrock technology story; current titles and later milestones require approval before publication.

media.alt: Founder spotlight featuring Patrick T. Prendergast, PhD, with a short scientific career summary and a path from invention to platform evolution.

nodes.title: Pipeline and What Comes Next
nodes.summary: PTP-102 is Byrock’s lead public program in equine laminitis, with continued development, evidence generation, and strategic advancement ahead. Broader platform or adjacent programs should appear only when approved for public disclosure, and no launch timing or market availability should be implied.

media.alt: Simple product pipeline display with PTP-102 highlighted as the lead public investigational program.
